note: Federated States of Micronesia: no noncitizen may enter or remain without an appropriate entry permit, and an alien worker's permit is issued to a noncitizen entering on compliance with all national laws on private or governmental employment, for the period the contract authorises (FSM Code 2014, title 50, ss. 102–103, read in archive.org's snapshot of 9 July 2016 of fsmlaw.org, which answers this client 406). Public Law 22-159 (14 October 2022) takes private-sector employees out of the Protection of Resident Workers Act (title 51, chapter 1) until 30 September 2027, so its labour certification isn't modelled now. Citizens of the United States need no permit for a visit of up to 365 days (s. 103(1)), but the code gives them no exemption from the alien worker's permit for employment, so they're under the same rule. A visitor's permit for short-term contractual services (s. 103(2)) and the states' own laws on nonresident workers aren't modelled apart, and no days without the permit are named. The Congress's lists of public laws from the 17th to the 24th Congress name no other change to title 50, chapter 1.

sources.title: Code of the Federated States of Micronesia (2014), title 50, chapter 1, Immigration Act, ss. 102–103 (archive.org snapshot of 9 July 2016)
sources.said: No noncitizen, vessel, or aircraft, unless specifically exempted by applicable law or regulations, shall enter or otherwise remain in the Federated States of Micronesia without having been issued an appropriate entry permit ... shall be issued to a noncitizen entering the Federated States of Micronesia upon compliance with all National laws relating to private or governmental employment for the period in which the employment of the alien worker is authorized by contract. ... with respect to citizens and nationals of the United States of America, for the effective period of the Compact of Free Association, and with respect to citizens and nationals of the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the Republic of Palau, a permit is not required for the duration of the visit, which shall not exceed 365 days.
